value: What published measurements exist of the cycle count and memory cost of post quantum and classical baseline signature and key establishment schemes on microcontroller class cores, for the gaps left after round 4: final standard SLH-DSA and FN-DSA, HQC, Cortex-M33, M55 and M85, RISC-V microcontroller cores, ESP32 class devices, stateful hash based signature verification, the overhead of implementations hardened against physical attacks, and the 168 MHz Ed25519 rows of Owens et al.

2026-10-20, before the first round 5 query was screened, as stated when the file was written. The git history does not evidence this timing: the file was first committed in the same commit as the search log, the screening file and the flow counts, and no hash of it is recorded in the repository (disclosed on 2026-10-21 after review)
publications of any year up to the search date; searches run on 2026-10-20 (UTC)
IACR ePrint and IACR TCHES (open access article pages and PDFs)
arXiv (public API, scripts/fetch_s13_arxiv.py, and arXiv PDFs)
IEEE Xplore abstract pages
ACM Digital Library abstract pages
web search engine in the style of Google Scholar (web search), including vendor and project pages
pqm4 benchmarks.csv at its current commit, fetched by git from github.com/mupq/pqm4

one backward round (reference lists of the 20 sources in data/bibliography.bib that the most evidence rows cite, where the full text was available) and one forward round (search engine queries naming those sources; Semantic Scholar pages if fetchable)
a cycle count, stack, RAM, code size or signature size value stated as a number in a table or an explicit sentence

measured on a microcontroller class core (Arm Cortex-M, ESP32 Xtensa or RISC-V microcontroller or soft core, Ibex, VexRiscv, RI5CY) or on such a core with accelerators, or an FPGA model of such a core

the scheme is a NIST selected or standardised post quantum scheme or its round predecessor, a classical baseline, or (for the hardened overhead question only) any lattice scheme with a published hardened and unhardened pair
the value is read from a retrieved full text, table or data file, never from an abstract or a summary alone
application processors (Cortex-A, x86, RV64 application cores such as C908) unless the row answers the hardened overhead question, where the core is stated in the comparability warning
values only in figures, times without a stated clock, or protocol level latencies without per operation cost
duplicates of rows already in data/evidence.csv
sources that could not be retrieved; refusals are recorded and not worked around
descriptions of attacks or of countermeasure techniques (only cost figures of hardened implementations are taken)
every staged row is read by two independent readers on blank sheets (scripts/verify6_sheets.py); every value and every wording disagreement gets a third look

2026-10-21, written after screening and after the review, disclosed: inclusion 5 (gap rule). A source is included only if at least one of its rows answers a named gap of the question: final standard SLH-DSA or FN-DSA, HQC, a Cortex-M33, M55 or M85 core, a RISC-V microcontroller core, an ESP32 class device, stateful hash based signature verification, a hardened and unhardened pair, or the 168 MHz Ed25519 rows of Owens et al. Screening already applied this rule ('outside the round 5 gap list') without it being written down; it is now applied to every source, which demoted the Falcon round 2 rows of Pornin 2019. A draft of this deviation also admitted provisional FN-DSA parameters while FIPS 206 is not final; review pass 2 (R2B09) noted that this clause widened the registered question after review, so it was removed: Falcon rows of a draft standard, such as those of ePrint 2026/1915, are not eligible until FIPS 206 is final and the rows match it

2026-10-21, after review: rows that break a written rule after double reading are demoted, not deleted: they stay in data/raw/S13_staged.csv and are listed with rule and reason in data/raw/S13_demoted.csv; scripts/promote_s13.py keeps them out of data/raw/S13_verified.csv
2026-10-21, after review: values read only through a summarising web fetch tool count as a summary under inclusion 4; such rows are demoted until the full text is read directly

2026-10-21, written after review pass 3 (R3B04), disclosed: a value from a line of a comparison table that cites earlier work is taken only when the source marks that line as its own measurement. One promoted row (S13-078) did not meet this and was demoted.
